summary: mountainash-rules is designed for extensibility across match strategies, aggregate operations, and backends. The codebase follows consistent patterns that make it straightforward to add new capabilities while maintaining cross-backend correctness.
use_cases: Add a new match strategy to support a domain-specific comparison (e.g., geographic proximity, semantic similarity).
Extend the accumulator engine with additional aggregate operations beyond sum.
Contribute cross-backend test coverage for new or existing strategies.
Improve expression compilation for better performance on a specific backend.

concepts.name: Adding a new MatchStrategy
concepts.description: The end-to-end process for a new strategy follows a clear path: add the enum value in constants.py, add validation logic in dimension.py, implement the _compile_ method in compiler.py, and add a corresponding test class. The design spec at docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-07-extended-match-strategies-design.md provides detailed guidance.

concepts.name: Adding an accumulator strategy
concepts.description: The AccumulatorCompiler currently supports EXACT, RANGE, GT, and LT strategies. To add support for additional strategies, implement the corresponding cases in compile_compatible (the compatibility guard) and compile_coalesce (the value-merge logic).

concepts.name: Adding a new aggregate operation
concepts.description: The Aggregate.operation field and the _expand_level method's agg_updates section define how accumulated values are combined. Currently sum is fully implemented; adding min, max, or product involves extending the agg_updates logic in _expand_level.

concepts.name: Backend-agnostic expression patterns
concepts.description: All compiler output uses the mountainash BaseExpressionAPI, ensuring expressions work across every supported backend. Use t_col, t_eq, t_ne and related helpers for sentinel-aware ternary comparisons, and ma.when/then/otherwise for conditional logic. Staying within these abstractions guarantees cross-backend compatibility.

concepts.name: Test patterns
concepts.description: Tests follow a consistent cross-backend parameterisation pattern. test_engine.py serves as the primary template for backend-parameterised evaluation tests, while test_accumulator_backends.py covers the accumulator engine. New strategies and features should follow these patterns to ensure coverage across all backends.
